node.title: Re: Creating arrays with glob patterns without metacharacters
node.author: haukex
node.doctext:
it could cause unintended and confusing side effects

It's of course a matter of opinion, but I do agree with this - it's a neat but somewhat obscure use of [doc://glob]. It can be useful, as it allows one to generate combinations using just core Perl, without loading e.g. [mod://Algorithm::Combinatorics]. But all it takes is someone who doesn't know the details ("If non-empty braces are the only wildcard characters used ...") or the interpolation of unchecked variables into the pattern for it to break. Personally, my feeling is that in a one-off script, or with a fixed string plus a comment warning future maintainers, it's ok to use. But if you want to play it safe with respect to future maintainers, I'd avoid it.

As for using as a replacement for qw/a b c/, sure it's clever, but IMO it's a silly place to save two characters, and I'd probably recommend against it. Also, I like to use File::Glob ':bsd_glob';, which breaks it:

$ perl -le 'print for ' a b c $ perl -MFile::Glob=:bsd_glob -le 'print for ' a b c
